en: All the things under discussion.
Many or most things.
Used as a placeholder verb to encapsulate a set of related verbs or any action.

everything.ety: Inherited from Middle English every thing; univerbation of every + thing.

ex.ja: 子供の頃は、周りのものが何でも大きく見えるものだ。

ex.ja: 君がしなさいと言う事は何でもする。

ex.en: The reporter took down everything that was said.
ex.ja: 記者は話されたことはすべて書き留めた。

en: Containing the maximum possible amount that can fit in the space available.
Complete; with nothing omitted.
Utmost measure or extent; highest state or degree; the state, position, or moment of fullness; fill.
The phase of the moon when its entire face is illuminated, full moon.
To become full or wholly illuminated.

ex.ja: その事務所は一日中活気に満ちていた。

en: To be alive; to have life.
To have permanent residence somewhere, to inhabit, to reside.
Having life; that is alive.
Being in existence; actual.
Of an event, as it happens; in real time; direct.
Of making a performance or speech, in person.

ex.ja: 君の家の近くに住めたらいいのに。

ex.ja: 空気がなかったら、すべての生き物は死ぬであろう。

ex.ja: 学校の近くに住んでいるので、普段は歩いて通学しています。

en: Something tiny, as a pinprick; a very small mark.
A full stop or other terminal punctuation mark.
Point taken; understood; got it.
To extend the index finger in the direction of something in order to show where it is or to draw attention to it.
To draw attention to something or indicate a direction.

point.ety:
From Middle English poynt, from Old French point m (“dot; minute amount”), from Latin pūnctum (“a hole punched in; a point, puncture”), substantive use of pūnctus m, perfect passive participle of pungō (“to prick, punch”); alternatively, from Old French pointe f (“sharp tip”), from Latin pūncta f (past participle), all from Proto-Italic *pungō (“to sting, prick”).
Mostly displaced native Middle English ord (“point”), from Old English ord (“point”). Doublet of pointe, ponto, puncto, punctum, punt, and punto.

ex.en: The stock price index was off 200 points yesterday.
ex.ja: 株価指数は昨日200ポイント下げた。

ex.en: I cannot agree with you on this point.
ex.ja: わたしはこの件に関しては君に同意できない。

ex.en: Everybody has some good points and bad points.
ex.ja: だれでも良い点と悪い点を持っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 punctum（突き刺した点）から。punct（刺す）。刺した跡 →「点・要点」、指先で刺すように示す →「指さす」。punctual（時間の点に正確な）も仲間。

en: To look at and interpret letters or other information that is written.
To be understood or physically read in a specific way.
A reading or an act of reading, especially of an actor's part of a play or a piece of stored data.
Something to be read; a written work.

ex.ja: 君は、是非ともその本を読むべきだ。

ex.ja: 君の興味をひく本なら何でも読んでいいよ。

en: To determine the number, amount, or value of [something].
To notice, discern. (Roughly, "can tell" means "know" but with a sense of direct perception.)
A reflexive, often habitual behavior, especially one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under ps…
A giveaway; something that unintentionally reveals or hints at a secret.

tell.ety:
From Middle English tellen (“to count, tell”), from Old English tellan (“to count, tell”), from Proto-West Germanic *talljan, from Proto-Germanic *taljaną, *talzijaną (“to count, enumerate”), from Proto-Germanic *talą, *talō (“number, counting”), from Proto-Indo-European *dol- (“calculation, fraud”).

ex.ja: 私は彼らにチケットをもう一枚送ってくれるように頼んだ。

ex.en: He told me the story of his life.
ex.ja: 彼は彼の人生の話を私にしてくれた。

ex.en: Tell them to call me before they leave.
ex.ja: 出発する前に私に電話するよう、彼らに伝えてください。

en: In negative or interrogative use, often with an expectation or potential of something happening in the future.
In negative imperative use, asking for an action to be delayed.
Nevertheless; however; but; despite that.

yet.ety: Inherited from Middle English yet, yit, from Old English ġīet, gȳta, from Proto-West Germanic *jūta, from Proto-Germanic *juta (compare West Frisian jit, jitte (“yet”), Dutch ooit (“ever”), German jetzt (“now”)), compound of (1) *ju (“already”, adverb), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yew-, accusative of *h₂óyu (“long time”) and (2) the Proto-Germanic *ta (“to, towards”), from Proto-Indo-European *do. More at aye and -th.

ex.en: I have yet to find a perfect husband.
ex.ja: 完璧な夫にまだ出会ったことがない。

ex.en: We have yet to learn all the facts.
ex.ja: われわれはまだ事実を十分に知らない。

ex.en: The full story was yet to be told.
ex.ja: まだ全部の話がされたわけではなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 gīet（今まで・それでも）から。「まだ」（時）と「けれども」（対比）。

Inaccurate; incorrect

ex.ja: 君は失敗を不運のせいにしてはいけない。

ex.en: We must always be prepared for the worst.
ex.ja: 我々は常に最悪の事態に備えていなければならない。

ex.en: We made the best of that bad situation.
ex.ja: 我々はあの悪い状況を極力生かした。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「悪い」。悪い、ひどい、下手な（bad at）、体に悪い（bad for）。比較級 worse、最上級 worst は別の語から補われた。

Describing a set or group with four elements.
The digit or figure 4; an occurrence thereof.
Anything measuring four units, as length.

Resistant to pressure; difficult to break, cut, or penetrate.
With much force or effort.
With difficulty.
A firm or paved beach or slope convenient for hauling vessels out of the water.
A tyre whose compound is softer than superhards, and harder than mediums.

ex.ja: 君の質問に僕は答えにくい。

ex.en: You must study hard and learn many things.
ex.ja: 君たちはしっかり勉強してたくさんのことを学ばなければなりません。

en: To intend, to plan (to do); to have as one's intention.
To have as intentions of a given kind.
Low in quality or degree; inferior; poor; shabby.
Without dignity of mind; destitute of honour; low-minded; spiritless; base.
A method or course of action used to achieve some result.
Something which is intermediate or in the middle; an intermediate value or range of values; a medium.

ex.ja: そういう印象を与えるつもりではなかったんです。

ex.en: You should by all means read the book.

en: One and only one time.
Formerly; during some period in the past.
As soon as; when; after.

once.ety: From Middle English ones, from Old English ānes, a remodelling (after ān (“one”)) of ǣnes, itself an extension of ǣne (“once”) with the genitive suffix -es. Equivalent to one + -s. Cognate with Saterland Frisian enst, insen (“once”), West Frisian iens (“once”), Dutch eens (“once”), German Low German eens, ins (“once”), German einst (“once”). ex.ja: 君は今すぐ出発せねばならない。

ex.en: You'd better have your hair cut at once.
ex.ja: 君はすぐ頭を刈ってもらったほうがいい。

ex.ja: 君はすぐにたばこをやめるべきだ。

en: To help keep from falling.
To back or favor a cause, party, etc., mentally or with concrete aid
Something which supports.
Financial or other help.

support.ety: From Middle English supporten, from Old French supporter, from Latin supportō.

ex.ja: 君はもう、自活できる年頃だ。

ex.en: At your age you ought to support yourself.
ex.ja: 君の年ならもう自活していてあたりまえだ。

ex.ja: 君の考えを立証する事実をあげてほしい。

en: To bring into a group, class, set, or total as a (new) part or member.
To consider as part of something; to comprehend.
A piece of source code or other content that is dynamically retrieved for inclusion in another item.

include.ety: From Middle English includen, borrowed from Latin inclūdere (“to shut in, enclose, insert”), from in- (“in”) + claudere (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂w- (“key, hook, nail”). Doublet of enclose. Displaced native Old English belūcan (“to include,” also “to shut in”).

ex.en: What's the price per night including all charges?
ex.ja: 税、その他全て込みだと１泊いくらですか。

ex.en: The stated price does not include labor charges.
ex.ja: 設定料金に労務費用は含みません。

ex.en: How much is it including insurance and tax?
ex.ja: 保険、税金を含めて、合計金額はいくらになりますか。

en: A series of sounds organized in time, usually employing some combination of harmony, melody, rhythm, tempo, timbre, sound design, lyrics,…
Any interesting or pleasing sounds.
To seduce or entice with music.

ex.ja: 君は禁煙するよう努力すべきだ。

ex.ja: 君は煙草を吸うのをやめることが必要だ。

ex.en: There is a bus stop near our school.
ex.ja: 学校の近くにバス停がある。

en: Something actual as opposed to invented.
Something which is real.
Used before making a statement to introduce it as a trustworthy one.

fact.ety: From Old French fact, from Latin factum (“an act, deed, feat, etc.”); also Medieval Latin for “state, condition, circumstance”; neuter of factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”). ex.en: You must state the fact as it is.
ex.ja: 君はその事実をありのまま述べなければならない。

ex.en: Show me a fact which supports your idea.
ex.ja: 君の考えを立証する事実をあげてほしい。

en: An effigy of a man burned on a bonfire on the anniversary of the Gunpowder Plot (5th November).
A man or boy; a fellow.
To exhibit an effigy of Guy Fawkes around the 5th November.
To make fun of, to ridicule with wit or innuendo.

guy.ety: Coined by semantic widening from the name of Guy Fawkes (1570–1606), an English Catholic executed for his role in the Gunpowder Plot, which also came to refer to effigies of his image burned annually on Guy Fawkes Night. The name Guy is from Old French Gui, from a Frankish form of Proto-West Germanic *Widō (compare Old Dutch Wido), a short form of names beginning with the element *widu (“wood”), from Proto-Germanic *widuz. Cognate with Italian Guido. Doublet of guido.

ex.ja: あいつには二度と会いたくない。

en: One of two usually roughly equal parts into which anything may be divided, or considered as divided.
One of two equal periods into which a game is divided.

ex.ja: メキシコの人口は日本の人口の半分です。

en: The capability for rational thought.

(construed with for) To design (an experiment) so that the effects of one or more variables are reduced or eliminated.

The method and means of governing the performance of any apparatus, machine or system, such as a lever, handle or button.

ex.en: Only six people were present at the party.
ex.ja: パーティーには６人しか出席しなかった。

ex.en: Every student has to leave school by six.
ex.ja: どの生徒も６時までに下校しなければならない。

note.ja: 古英語 siex から。ラテン語 sex（sextet）、ギリシャ語 hex（hexagon）と同じ祖先。

en: The direction opposite to that of the earth's rotation, specifically 270°.
The western region or area; the inhabitants thereof.
Situated or lying in or toward the west; westward.
Of wind: from the west.
Towards the west; westwards.
To move to the west; (of the sun), to set.

west.ety:
PIE word
 *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros
From Middle English west, from Old English west, from Proto-West Germanic *westr (“western”), from Proto-Germanic *westrą (“west”), from Proto-Germanic *westraz (“west”), from Proto-Indo-European *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros (“evening”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots wast (“west”), North Frisian waast, weest, wäst (“west”), Saterland Frisian Wääste (“west”), West Frisian and Dutch west (“west”), German West (“west”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk vest (“west”), Faroese and Icelandic vestur (“west”), Swedish väst, väster (“west”); also with Irish feascar, feasgar (“even

ex.en: Many men went west in search of gold.
ex.ja: 金を探し求めて大勢の人々が西にむかった。

ex.en: The island lies to the west of Japan.
ex.ja: その島は日本の西方にある。

ex.en: The company is located on the West Coast.
ex.ja: その会社は西海岸にあります。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「夕方・日の沈む方角」。ラテン語 vesper（夕方）と同じ祖先。

en: Agreement of opinion, will, or action.
Agreement in pitch and tone; harmony, musical concord.
To make to agree or correspond; to suit one thing to another; to adjust.
To bring (people) to an agreement; to reconcile, settle, adjust or harmonize.

accord.ety: From Middle English accord, from Old French acort, from acorder (see verb below).

ex.en: You will be paid according to your ability.
ex.ja: 給料は君の能力次第だ。

ex.en: The conference went off according to the plan.
ex.ja: 会議は計画どおりに運んだ。

ex.en: According to the radio, it will snow tomorrow.
ex.ja: ラジオによれば、明日は雪になるそうです。

note.ja: ac（〜へ）+ cord（心）。心を〜に合わせる →「一致（する）」。according to（〜に一致して→〜によれば）。record（心に呼び戻す→記録する）、cordial（心からの）も同じ cor。

en: Such as one may avail oneself of; capable of being used for the accomplishment of a purpose.
Readily obtainable.

available.ety: From Middle English available, avayllable, avayleable, equivalent of avail + -able.

ex.en: Will the room be available for the meetings?
ex.ja: その部屋を会議に使うことはできますか。

ex.en: We have little money available for the research.
ex.ja: その研究に使える金はほとんどないんだ。

ex.en: This book is available at one shop only.
ex.ja: この本はただ一軒の店でだけ入手できる。

note.ja: a（〜へ）+ vail（強い・価値がある）+ able。役に立つ価値がある →「利用できる・手が空いている」。value と同じ val。
